While tracking elephants in Namibia's Huab River Valley, Veronesi spotted an unusual trail of drag marks across the sand of a dry riverbed. Following the tracks, he came across a female elephant carrying a dead calf, its leg wedged between her tusk and trunk. Initially, Veronesi assumed the elephant was the calf's mother. But after sharing his photographs with an elephant research project working in the area, he learned that this wasn't certain. Researchers recognised the elephant as a female who had lost a calf several years earlier and said she had previously picked up dead calves belonging to other females. For Veronesi, the encounter was deeply significant. "Of all the 20 years I've done photographing animals, this is the most heart-wrecking and fascinating and dramatic," he said, describing it as "revealing of the depth and complexity of the emotions, the feelings of the animals." He hopes the image will encourage people to look beyond animals' physical appearance and recognise them as individuals with their own relationships, memories and emotions. "It's a small window that opens just a crack into the complexity of their world," he said. news.full_article_text: Madras HC asks Tamil Nadu police why RSS annual route march permission is denied every year Madras High Court asked the Tamil Nadu police why the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) was denied permission to hold its annual route march in the state The Madras High Court on Wednesday asked the Tamil Nadu police why the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) was denied permission to hold its annual route march in the state, irrespective of the party in power. If the “State of Jammu and Kashmir” could allow meetings or marches by the RSS, “why Tamil Nadu can not have it?” Justice V Lakshminarayanan said. “What is your fear? Every year they (RSS) are coming (for permission) amd the Court is granting. What is so exceptional in 2026? Has there been any violence so far in their march?” the high court asked. “State is looking at citizens as enemies, what to do?” Justice Lakshminarayanan remarked, adding that successive governments had rejected such requests. The court was hearing a petition filed by RSS North Tamil Nadu secretary VG Jagadeesan, challenging police orders denying permission for marches scheduled across the state. Jagadeesan’s plea sought permission for RSS route marches on October 18 and 25 and November 1. The petitioner proposed that participants wear the organisation’s uniform and march alongside a musical band, followed by public meetings. Advocate general Vijay Narayan argued that the routes proposed for the RSS marches were unsuitable and that permitting the processions during the festive season would “inconvenience the public, particularly those out shopping for Diwali and Navratri.” Narayan said the marches would also require substantial police deployment at a time when the authorities had other responsibilities. The judge questioned the need for repeated litigation over permissions for processions and suggested that the state should enact legislation if it intended to prohibit them altogether. “Pass a legislation saying no person will be entitled to take a procession or a march if the State is insistent on denying permission,” the high court said. Senior advocate NL Rajah, appearing for the petitioner, argued that the RSS had conducted annual marches since its inception in 1925. He also submitted that procedural guidelines governing processions did not constitute inflexible statutory requirements and that the police should seek clarifications from organisers instead of rejecting applications outright. Rajah objected to police orders referring to mosques along the proposed routes, arguing that such reasoning undermined Tamil Nadu’s communal harmony. Justice Lakshminarayanan also said that the presence of places of worship along a route should not, by itself, justify refusing permission. Advocate general Narayan argued that the proposed routes were unsuitable and that the marches could inconvenience the public during the festive season. He also cited the substantial police deployment that the events would require. The court directed the petitioner’s counsel to meet state public prosecutor R John Sathyan on Wednesday to discuss the dates, timings and routes, and report the outcome on October 15. news.headline: Thousands march to Indian Supreme Court to demand election chief resign
news.story_lead: India's opposition party members march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in Delhi - Published 12 October 2026 Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend.
news.full_article_text: India's opposition party members march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in Delhi - Published 12 October 2026 Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi submitted a petition to the court challenging the process, in which tens of millions of names have been struck off the voter rolls. Opposition parties allege the revision benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission and the BJP reject the charge. For weeks requests to protest had been denied by police, citing law and order reasons. Attempts to hold a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) pressure group over the weekend led to thousands of demonstrators being detained in Delhi. Gandhi called "all opposition parties, civil society groups [and] all those who believe in democracy" to join Monday's march. In a press conference, he shared a letter that he and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge had written to Chief Justice Surya Kant, laying out their concerns with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's alleged conduct. After they filed their petition later in the day, Kant responded by saying the matter was already before the court and therefore sub judice - meaning he could not speak about it. But he added: "You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law." There was a heavy security deployment in central Delhi and along the route of the march, with restrictions on traffic and on entry and exit at some metro stations. A bus carrying Gandhi and other opposition leaders made its way to the court from Barakamba road. Supporters waved flags and chanted his name as the Congress MP and others waved through the windows. Seated a few rows behind him was Neha Bora, a student leader who has gained prominence in the protests. A few kilometres on, in a place called Mandi House, the bus stopped and Rahul Gandhi and a few others climbed on top of the vehicle to wave at supporters lining up the street in the thousands. Many protesters climbed on to other buses parked here, while some waved flags and chanted anti-government slogans to the sound of drums and lots of cheering. "If they take away our right to vote, what is left with us?" one protester asked an AFP news agency reporter. Another protester called the march "a fight to save the very fabric" of India, the world's largest democracy. Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi holds up a copy of India's Constitution at a press conference on Monday Protesters have been demanding the country's the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud Over the past week, top opposition leaders, including Gandhi, have been briefly detained several times while leading protests in central Delhi. On Sunday, the CJP - which is not a registered political party - said it would continue protesting until Kumar stepped down. The CJP, which successfully led a protest over the summer that culminated in India's federal education minister's resignation, had called for a march on Saturday to Jantar Mantar - the best-known protest site in Delhi where the last set of sit-in demonstrations had also happened. But authorities in Delhi imposed overarching restrictions that made it almost impossible for protesters to travel and reach Jantar Mantar - trains were cancelled, dozens of metro stations were shut and tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were on the roads to detain protesters. The Home Ministry has now announced demonstrations will no longer be permitted at Jantar Mantar. Three other sites have been listed as alternatives should permission be granted. Monday's demonstrations come after thousands were detained over the weekend The CJP leaders - founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - were dramatically detained from a plane as they landed in Delhi to join the weekend protest. They were only released a day later - while Dipke returned home to attend his grandmother's funeral, Das and Ranka held a press conference where they said the protests would continue. Both leaders have said they will seek a new protest date from the police. Over the weekend, the police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists. Some videos and photos from the protest show police dragging people, including women, by force and pushing them into buses. The BBC also captured footage , external of a policeman slapping a detained protester inside a bus. The Delhi police did not respond to questions about the use of violence against protesters. In a statement, Reporters Without Borders condemned the detention of at least 16 Indian journalists. "Covering events of public interest is not a crime. It is their job. The police's actions against the press are unacceptable," it said. Rahul Gandhi said that young Indians who had come to peacefully protest with "love in their hearts, not hatred or anger" had been beaten up. BJP President Nitin Nabin accused opposition parties and the CJP of trying to destabilise India "at the behest of foreign forces" without elaborating on who the forces were. Related topics

news.full_article_text: Supreme Court asks Centre, states to reply to plea seeking ban on sale of alcohol in tetra packs, sachets Nair said these tetra packs appear like fruit juice with alcohol content mentioned in smaller letters. The Supreme Court on Wednesday asked the Centre and states to file their response in four weeks on a plea for banning the sale of alcohol in "inconspicuous packaging" such as tetra packs and sachets. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, R Mahadevan and Aparesh Kumar Singh gave the petitioner NGO 'Community Against Drunken Driving' two weeks to file its rejoinder thereafter and listed the matter for detailed hearing after six weeks. Senior advocate Vipin Nair, appearing for the NGO, said alcoholic beverages being sold in tetra packs in 10 states and Union Territories (UTs) have deceptive imagery with names like 'Chili Mango Vodka'. He said these tetra packs appear like fruit juice with alcohol content mentioned in smaller letters. Nair said the Centre and states have not filed their response to the petition. The bench ordered, "Liberty is granted to the petitioner to serve the unserved respondents through the standing counsel for the concerned respondents... Four weeks' time is granted to the represented respondent(s) to file their counter affidavit(s). "The petitioner will have two weeks' time thereafter to file a rejoinder affidavit. List the matter after six weeks." The plea sought a direction to the Centre to frame a policy applicable to all states and UTs and to ban the sale of alcohol in packaging such as tetra packs and sachets. It also sought a direction to the Centre to frame a policy in respect of the states to amend their respective excise Acts, rules and policies forthwith, adopting uniform definitions of "bottling" limited to glass containers or other visibly distinct receptacles. The petition said there should be standardisation and harmonisation of excise policies of different states regarding the bottling of liquor. It said inconspicuous packaging had the potential to dramatically increase the public consumption of alcohol. "The petitioner is constrained to file this public interest petition after observing that alcohol, particularly cheaper alcohol, is being sold in inconspicuous packaging viz portable PET bottles, plastic sachets and tetra packs in various states across the nation," it said. Senior advocate Arvind Datar, appearing for Action Alliance for Recycling Beverage Cartons (AARC), sought impleadment of the petitioner and said that in the garb of a public interest litigation (PIL), the instant matter is specifically, directly and categorically targeted at the paper-based carton packaging industry since the entire petition has been premised on the argument that purportedly the sale of liquor in glass bottles is better than the sale of liquor in aseptic paper-based carton packages. The AARC said that liquor/ alcoholic beverages have been permitted to be sold in aseptic paper-based cartons in India for the past 21 years, and are presently so permitted in 10 states and UTs. "For example, the state of Karnataka has permitted such sales since 2005, the state of Andhra Pradesh since 2014 and the state of Uttar Pradesh since 2014. It is stated that state excise policies in this regard have been issued openly and in exercise of statutory power, and have continued uninterrupted since," it said. The plea of AARC said at present, an estimated 10 billion packs of alcoholic beverage cartons are being sold in India in a year. "It is stated that where a lawful practice has subsisted openly, under statutory permission, for almost 21 years, and where investment and employment on that scale have been created in reliance upon it, a petition seeking its prohibition without any explanation for the delay in challenging the same, is liable to be dismissed on the ground of delay and laches and more so where the relief would have an immediate and irreversible prejudice upon a large body of third parties not before the court," it said. The bench allowed the impleadment of AARC in the matter. The top court also asked the Centre and the states to file their responses in four weeks on the plea of the NGO for direction for an effective protocol and robust policy for the enforcement of mandatory age checks at liquor sales points. It directed that a copy be served to the office of Solicitor General Tushar Mehta for his response. "List the matter after six weeks. In the meantime, the petitioner may serve a copy of this petition in the office of the solicitor general. "Four weeks' time is granted to the respondent no. 1, Union of India, to file a counter affidavit," it said. On May 20, the top court sought responses from the Centre and other stakeholders on a plea for a ban on the sale of alcohol in tetra packs and sachets. On November 11, 2024, the top court sought a response from the Centre on a petition by the NGO which said that the excise policy of different states has age legislation making it illegal to consume or possess alcohol below a certain age but a robust mechanism to check the age of consumers or buyers at alcohol points of sale or consumption is absent. The petition has also opposed doorstep delivery of liquor service, contending it would hasten the formation of the habit of alcohol consumption among underage persons.

Granting four weeks for the Centre to file its response to the petition filed by an organisation, Community Against Drunken Driving, a bench headed by justice Vikram Nath said that despite notice being issued on the petition in May, no response had been filed by the Centre, nor had any lawyer appeared on behalf of the central government. “We grant four weeks to the Union of India to file its counter affidavit. In the meantime, the petitioner may serve a copy of the paper book on the office of the solicitor general. List after six weeks,” the bench, also comprising justices R Mahadevan and Aparesh Kumar Singh, said. Deep Dive The petition was argued by advocate Vipin Nair, who said, “It seems the Centre is not very serious about the issue.” He said that the packaged alcohol had deceptive names and pictures which attracted minors to consume the drink. “It is alarming that these tetra packs are marketed under labels such as ‘Bunty Premium Vodka’, ‘Chilli Mango Vodka’, and ‘Premium Romanov Vodka – Apple Thrill’, clearly intended to mislead consumers. The use of fruit names alongside colour photographs of apples and mangoes on the packaging further reinforces this deception,” the petition said. The petition was opposed by the Action Alliance for Recycling Beverage Cartons (AARC), a society comprising companies engaged in the packaging business, including those selling alcoholic beverages. An application filed by AARC was argued by senior advocate Arvind Datar, who stated that there was no harm in selling alcoholic beverages in tetra packs and sachets, as such packaging avoids adulteration and cannot be recycled. He further pointed out that such packages are allowed under the prevailing excise laws in 10 states. Datar showed samples of alcoholic beverages and said that health is a state subject and that excise also falls under the jurisdiction of states. The court allowed AARC to be part of the proceedings and granted the association time to file its response to the petition. It also directed the states to respond. Nair said that his petition also seeks mandatory age verification, as the sale of alcohol is prohibited to persons below 18 years of age. The PIL stated that unlike cigarette packs and tobacco sachets, which carry statutory warnings, these packs carry no such labels, and even where warnings are present, they are barely visible. These drinks masquerade as fruit juice, and such packaging facilitates easy access and concealment, encourages underage consumption, promotes public drinking and drunk driving, and even enables smuggling across state borders, it added. The petitioner NGO, which has been actively pursuing a campaign against drunken driving, said that the issue needs to be tackled legally because the definitions of “bottling” and “bottle” under different state excise acts are “broad and varying”, with a bottle encompassing pots, baskets, flasks, wrappers and other similar receptacles. As a result, liquor is available in portable PET bottles, plastic sachets and tetra packs across states. The petition stated that states’ discretion in defining bottles should be guided by environmental and health concerns, rather than solely by the revenue such sales would generate for state coffers. The petition added that the Central Excise law also provides no help in this regard. “It is apparent that the excise authorities in various states have allowed liquor to be packaged and sold in inconspicuous packaging. Such packages are very easy to sneak into public places such as parks, educational institutes, and cinema halls. Even children cannot be spotted easily if they consume liquor from such packages,” the petition said. These packs are cheap, encouraging young, impressionable minds to purchase and consume more, the petition said, urging the court to lay down uniform guidelines to protect the health and lives of citizens.

news.full_article_text: CEC an institution, not a person, won't enjoy any special privilege: Ex-Supreme Court justice Justice Joseph invoked concerns raised during the Constituent Assembly debates about the integrity of those responsible for conducting elections. Former Supreme Court judge Justice Kurian Joseph has stressed that the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) must not enjoy any special privilege as an individual, arguing that authority should rest with the institution rather than the person holding the office. He called for stronger constitutional safeguards to protect the independence and integrity of the Election Commission of India (ECI). “CEC by himself shall not enjoy any special privilege. It is meant to be an institution, not a person. Unfortunately, people holding high constitutional office in our country have, according to me, what they call a misguided impression that there is power concentrated on the person...If it is an institutional exercise of that power, you will have to think twice, he said, as per LiveLaw . Justice Joseph made the remarks while delivering the inaugural address at a seminar titled “Independence of Election Commission of India: Compromised?”, organised by the Indian Association of Lawyers, Keralam. He argued that the appointment of Election Commissioners and the conditions governing their service should be protected through constitutional provisions rather than left to parliamentary legislation. ‘Has democracy been poisoned at its source?’ Justice Joseph invoked concerns raised during the Constituent Assembly debates about the integrity of those responsible for conducting elections. Referring to Constituent Assembly member Hriday Nath Kunzru, he warned that a lack of trust in the officials overseeing elections could undermine democracy itself. “Dr. Hriday Nath Kunzru spoke about the integrity of the person who is holding that office. And if that integrity is not impeccable, then democracy will be poisoned at the source. Is this not what we see in the days that we have been passing through? Has the democracy not been poisoned at the hands of people who have not been acting in accordance with the vision of the Constitution? So, therefore, my dear friends, I would only say these are the times that the country should think about and take steps for protection of our democracy. And if such constitutional powers are vested in great institutions like the Election Commission of India, its integrity and independence should be ensured as well”, he was quoted as saying by Live Law. He maintained that protecting the ECI's independence was essential given the constitutional responsibilities entrusted to it. Justice Joseph seeks safeguards for appointment and removal of Election Commissioners The former judge called for the Constitution to lay down the appointment procedures and service conditions of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners. He also proposed that all Election Commissioners should be removable only through the same procedure applicable to Supreme Court judges. Referring to Article 324 of the Constitution, Justice Joseph noted that it gives the ECI superintendence, direction and control over the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections. However, he questioned whether the existing constitutional framework provided sufficient safeguards to ensure the independence of the institution. news.full_article_text: Rahul, Priyanka join Ankita Bhandari's family's protest against ‘VIP’ Sikkim governor's appointment Ankita Bhandari, a resident of Uttarakhand, worked as a receptionist at Vanantra Resort in Yamkeshwar, near Rishikesh. She was murdered in 2022. Congress leaders Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra met the parents of Ankita Bhandari in New Delhi on Wednesday evening. Together, they staged a sit-in near India Gate against the appointment of former Uttarakhand BJP in-charge Dushyant Kumar Gautam as the Governor of Sikkim. The parents of the 19-year-old receptionist, who was murdered in Uttarakhand’s Pauri Garhwal district in September 2022, have demanded that Gautam’s appointment be put on hold until the ongoing Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the alleged VIP angle in the case was completed. Activist Yogita Bhayana also joined the protest, during which Ankita’s parents requested President Droupadi Murmu to intervene and ensure that the investigation examined all allegations related to the case. Gautam served as the BJP’s Uttarakhand in-charge from November 2020 to August 2026, a period during which the party recorded several electoral victories in the state. He was appointed Sikkim governor on Monday. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi voiced support for Ankita Bhandari’s parents and accused the BJP of protecting a “VIP” accused in the case. On X, Rahul said the family had been waiting for justice for four years, alleging that the accused had instead received protection and a constitutional position. “I and the Congress Party stand with them — in their grief as well as in this fight for justice,” he said. Ankita’s parents demand investigation into alleged VIP role Speaking to the media during the protest, Ankita’s father demanded action against Gautam and called for the statements of actress Urmila Sanawar and former BJP MLA Suresh Rathore to be included in the investigation. “Dushyant Kumar should go to jail...because of the VIP my daughter was murdered,” he told HT. He questioned the progress of the CBI investigation, alleging that it relied on statements made by witnesses in the lower court. He also claimed that the call details of the accused had not been examined. “I request the President not to appoint Dushyant Kumar as governor until the CBI investigation is complete,” he said. “Even though the CBI probe is underway, it is depending on the statements of witnesses in lower court. Statements of Urmila Sanawar and Suresh Rathore should be included in the investigation. The call details of the accused were not examined.” Ankita’s mother also appealed to the President to reconsider the appointment. “We were hurt by the appointment of Kumar as governor. I request the President, who is a woman and will understand my sentiments, to halt the appointment of Kumar as governor,” she said. The family has sought a thorough investigation into the alleged involvement of a VIP in Ankita’s murder. Gautam has not been named as an accused in the cases related to the crime, and the allegations against him remain unproven. Audio clip triggered demands for CBI probe The demand for a fresh investigation into the alleged VIP angle gained momentum after actress Urmila Sanawar, who claims to be the wife of former BJP MLA Suresh Rathore, released an audio clip purportedly containing a telephone conversation between the two. In the recording, Rathore allegedly referred to the involvement of a BJP leader in the case. The clip triggered protests across Uttarakhand, with demonstrators demanding a CBI investigation into the alleged role of the unidentified VIP. Following the protests, the Uttarakhand government ordered a CBI probe in January. Gautam has denied allegations linking him to the murder and filed a case against Rathore, Sanawar, the Uttarakhand unit of the Congress, Uttarakhand Kranti Dal, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and other unidentified individuals over claims connecting him to the case. The Delhi High Court has also directed the removal of social media posts linking Gautam to the murder, observing that the allegations appeared prima facie defamatory, HT reported earlier. Congress protests Gautam’s appointment The protest at India Gate came a day after the Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee (UKPCC), led by its president Ganesh Godiyal, held a silent demonstration in Dehradun against Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim governor. The Congress has questioned the decision to appoint Gautam while demands for an investigation into the alleged VIP angle remain unresolved. The party has called for accountability and further scrutiny of the allegations. The Congress accused the BJP-led Centre of protecting Gautam following his appointment as Sikkim governor, alleging that the decision undermined the demand for justice in the 2022 Ankita Bhandari murder case. On X, the party said Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra met Ankita’s family at India Gate in New Delhi. “The allegation was that pressure was put on Ankita to provide services to Dushyant Gautam. When Ankita refused, she was murdered,” the Congress alleged. It accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of rewarding Gautam with the gubernatorial appointment despite the allegations against him. “The daughters and women of the country are watching how Narendra Modi and his government are protecting Dushyant Gautam. Instead of delivering justice to Ankita Bhandari, the entire BJP government is bent on silencing the voice of the victim's family,” the Congress wrote. What happened to Ankita Bhandari? Ankita, a resident of Uttarakhand’s Pauri Garhwal district, worked as a receptionist at Vanantra Resort in Yamkeshwar, near Rishikesh. She was murdered on September 18, 2022. The resort’s owner, Pulkit Arya, son of expelled BJP leader Vinod Arya, and his two employees, Saurabh Bhaskar and Ankit Gupta, were convicted in the case.
